source_signature.notes: Batch 4F skill 3/5. Scope Operator-derived. The CONTRAST skill to the trusses just signed: a frame or machine contains at least one multi-force member (loaded at more than two points, between its end connections, or by an applied couple), so its pin force is NOT axial — it has two unknown components, unlike a two-force member whose direction two_force_member_identification fixed. This is the FBD and modeling step; solving is frame_machine_equilibrium (skill 4/5), the ceiling, which lists this node as a prerequisite. Synthesis of three signed parents, verified woven: two_force_member_identification (the two-force test, so the multi-force contrast is sharp and a two-force link inside a frame can reduce unknowns), support_reaction_modeling (external reaction components), rigid_body_fbd_2d (how to draw one body's FBD, extended here to dismembered members with pin-interaction forces). The skill owns Newton's third law at each internal pin as a DRAWING rule: the pair on the two adjoining member FBDs is equal and opposite. REVIEW-BEAT CORRECTION, a genuine pedagogy defect not mere wording: the first draft's only internal pin (B) connected multi-force AB to TWO-FORCE BD. Because BD is two-force, the force at B lies along BD — one unknown, not two — and the draft conceded as much in its own solution. The example therefore never demonstrated the two-component pin force that is the entire point of the skill, and it contradicted its own concept (which says a two-force member inside a frame REDUCES unknowns, then drew two components at exactly the reducing pin). Root cause is structural: in any two-member frame with one two-force member the shared pin is always adjacent to it and thus constrained. Redesigned so BOTH members are multi-force — AB vertical with a horizontal load H at midheight, BC horizontal with a downward load P at midspan, joined at internal pin B — so neither is two-force and the pin force at B is a genuine two-component unknown, Operator-verified on disk. 3-signal mapping, all genuinely EARNED and the OPPOSITE of the Decision B count-and-classify debt, because this is the first 4F skill that actually places and resolves forces: axis_confusion at step 4 (mislabeling which of the two rectangular pin components is x versus y — a real error only because the components are now independent, not locked to a member axis), sign_or_placement_error at step 5 (drawing the Newton's-third-law pair with the same sense instead of opposite), unclassified at step 6 (misclassification, incomplete FBD, importing a solve). simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Hard stops verified absent: no equilibrium equations solved, no pin/reaction/member magnitude found, no method of joints or sections, no truss determinacy count, no 3D. This lane also recorded a third cross-phase pattern for the Architect: an identification/FBD skill's worked example must EXERCISE the skill's distinguishing feature, not merely include it — the same defect family as contact_force_modeling's single interface and two_force_member_identification's single member, here the constrained pin. Caught and corrected before sign-off.
